evidence.claim: The claim that GP-MILP yields MILP-equivalent solutions is inconsistent, since pruning unavoidably removes some oracle-active links, with no evidence presented that this does not harm optimality.
evidence.excerpt: GP-MILP "MILP-equivalent" claim vs. 99% recall pruning is not fully consistent. Sec. VI.D states pruning is done at τ=0.15 to retain oracle-active links "with high probability (99%)", then claims GP-MILP preserves "MILP-equivalent solutions (same objective value)". Since 1% of the oracle-active links are, by construction, pruned away, GP-MILP cannot in general reach the exact optimum on those instances; either the claim needs re-scoping (e.g. "on X% of validation instances") or evidence must be given that alternative equally-optimal solutions always exist within the pruned graph.

judge_panel.reason: The paper claims GP-MILP 'preserves MILP-equivalent solutions on the evaluated dataset, i.e., yielding the same objective value' while also stating pruning retains oracle-active links 'with high probability (99%)'. The paper appears to be making an empirical claim verified on the dataset rather than a theoretical guarantee, but does not clarify what fraction of instances were affected by the 1% miss rate, leaving the consistency of the claim unclear.

The paper does not make a universal guarantee; it explicitly scopes the claim empirically: "Experimental results demonstrate that GP-MILP ... [preserves] MILP-equivalent solutions on the evaluated dataset, i.e., yielding the same objective value and connectivity outcome as the MILP solved on the complete graphs" (Sec. VI.D). The simultaneous statement that pruning retains oracle-active links "with high probability (99%)" is not logically inconsistent with dataset-level objective equivalence.

The paper asserts that GP-MILP preserves 'MILP-equivalent solutions on the evaluated dataset' (Sec. VI.D) despite pruning at a 99% recall threshold, but provides no empirical breakdown or theoretical justification to explain how optimality is maintained when 1% of oracle-active links are discarded.
